officialReferences.use: Current index distinguishes styled elements from primitives; this research does not upgrade installed API.
Manual activation permits arrow/Home/End focus changes without selection. Closing a tab should restore logical focus. This is guidance, not a claim of full assistive-technology conformance.

sourceObservations.finding: Actual Thread import/render present. referenceComponents at line49 includes MessageActions and ComposerActions but no MessageFooter.

MessageFooter lines88-107 returns a fixed draft status early for assistant draft; otherwise requires taskId and role=user before any PluginView/AppSlot. Final assistant messages do not render this registered footer slot.
Actual Thread components expose MessageFooter and call it for assistant at line693 and user at line802. The coverage restriction is in host integration, not absence of the Thread seam.

Menu uses position:absolute under position:relative; Arc tab strip has overflow:auto. Potential popup clipping/scroll interaction requires actual observation; source alone does not prove a visible defect.

interpretation.messageFooter: Confirmed static contribution coverage gap relative to user requirement that all relevant interface regions be extensible. Existing built-in stream/activity presentation may intentionally be user-message-specific; do not blindly remove the role gate and duplicate built-in content.
interpretation.menu: Unverified geometry risk only; do not relabel current passing split/close behavior as failed or request a new standalone browser run based on this static inference.
interpretation.keyboard: Current Arc focusTab changes focus only for arrow/Home/End; App closeNow and closeWorkspaceNow already schedule focus restoration. No new focus-loss finding from this read.
interpretation.reducedMotion: Global styles.css:590 disables animations/transitions and smooth scroll for reduced motion; local skeleton wrapper classes alone are not evidence of a motion defect.

recommendedExistingPlanFollowup: Under the original plugin integration owner and existing plan, separate general message-footer contribution rendering from built-in per-role stream/status eligibility; preserve scoped task/message identity and capability guards.
Explicitly document which task and conversation message states expose the slot; ensure generic task Thread uses the same host seam if it is part of supported coverage.

Use a small contribution visible on an assistant final and user message when an authorized affected verification segment is naturally available; built-in activity must not duplicate and revoked/unmounted context must not run actions.
Keep current Arc visual and login delivery first. Do not add another registry, arbitrary DOM injection, third task layer, or changes to the current frozen browser inputs.
limitations: No runtime plugin activation or mounted message footer check performed.
No screenshot of an open Arc overflow menu inspected in this research.
